items.name: amazing-sandbox
items.source_story_title: Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace
items.summary: An ephemeral container sandbox for coding agents, endorsed for limiting filesystem exposure.
items.why_included: A concrete first-hand sandbox recommendation emerged from the extension-compromise discussion.
items.evidence: The commenter runs the sandbox with access to the working directory and says it drastically limits the attack radius.

evidence_sources.author: ashishb
evidence_sources.excerpt: I run it in an ephemeral container sandbox (https://github.com/ashishb/amazing-sandbox) which has access to the current working directory and it drastically limits the attack radius.

items.name: rhun
items.source_story_title: Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
items.summary: A lightweight code editor written in assembly, praised by a daily fork user.
items.why_included: The commenter explicitly praises the editor and distinguishes their scratchpad fork from the upstream project.
items.evidence: The commenter calls the assembly editor good and minimalist, and says they use their scratchpad fork daily.

evidence_sources.author: Imustaskforhelp
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is an genuinely good minimalist good editor that is created in mostly assembly that was created with the help of AI[0] I maintain a fork of it which basically adds scratchpad ability to it and is something that I use daily myself for what it's worth[1]

items.name: Florilegium
items.summary: A procedural flower generator for LaTeX, inspiring a commenter's seeded daily-note decorations.
items.why_included: The endorsement includes a concrete creative adaptation rather than a bare project mention.
items.evidence: The commenter praises the flowers and reports converting the project into an Obsidian extension seeded by note filenames.

evidence_sources.author: ClaraForm
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is beautiful, thank you! I just asked Deepseek 4.1 Flash to convert it to an Obsidian extension that uses the file-name as the seed, and the result [1] is exactly something I've been dreaming of for so many years while I take daily notes.

items.name: Astroterm
items.source_story_title: Astroterm: A Planetarium for Your Terminal
items.summary: A terminal planetarium that one user made into a location-aware screensaver.
items.why_included: A working screensaver setup supplies unusually tangible first-hand praise.
items.evidence: The commenter installed Astroterm as an Omarchy screensaver, says it tracks their local sky, and calls it awesome.

evidence_sources.author: jubalizer
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is really cool. I've managed to set this up as my default screensaver in Omarchy. It tracks the sky from my house. Awesome!
